subject: Urgent: Brightline production errors — cross-region route & DNS anomalies
messages:
From: Alex Morales <alex.morales@brightlineretail.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production errors and timeouts across checkout region (Brightline)

Hi Vivek / team,

We're seeing elevated 5xx errors and long tail latency in our US-west checkout traffic starting ~14:00 UTC. Error spikes correlate with increased DNS lookup times and intermittent TCP retransmits. Impact: checkout failures for ~12% of sessions and page load times up ~3s for affected users.

We attached a short pcap and an initial traceroute from our edge to your inference endpoint. Can you please triage immediately? Our ops lead is looped here. This is affecting peak revenue minutes.

Attachments: packet_capture_brightline_20260822.pcap (pcap) | route_trace_brightline_20260822.txt (text)

Thanks,
Alex Morales
Head of Platform Ops
Brightline Retail

+1 415-555-0198
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 15:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors and timeouts across checkout region (Brightline)

Alex — thanks for the quick flag and for attaching the captures. I'm escalating this to network and infra immediately.

Sean: can you take point on the packet capture and traceroute? Please correlation-check (1) VPC peering health between us and Brightline's VPC, (2) any known NGFW/proxy rules that may be rate-limiting or injecting latency, (3) our regional DNS resolvers in us-west.

Marissa / Hannah: I want a customer-facing update within 30 minutes with what we know and the mitigation path. Include SLA workaround (route bypass or fallback model pool) and request their permission to failover traffic if we identify a bad intermediate path.

I'll loop leadership if this looks like an extended outage.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Morales <alex.morales@brightlineretail.com>, Nitin Rao <nitin@cloudpeers.io>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors and timeouts across checkout region (Brightline)

Quick triage notes (preliminary):
- Packet captures show a high rate of NXDOMAIN and repeated 4xx from Brightline's recursive resolver clusters between 14:00-15:30 UTC. DNS latency spikes to ~1.2s on some lookups.
- Traceroute shows an asymmetric path: a mid-hop in the cloud-peers backbone is introducing ~120-180ms extra RTT and intermittent packet loss. The path then returns to expected latency beyond that hop, suggesting a peering or transit issue rather than our origin.
- No immediate evidence of our NGFW dropping or injecting; our egress proxies logged elevated SYN retransmits toward Brightline's edge but not drops from our side.

Immediate actions taken:
1) Opened a support ticket with CloudPeers (cc: Nitin) — requested rapid packet-forward and confirmation of peering health for the time window.
2) Temporarily enabled route bypass to our secondary us-west model pool to force traffic along an alternate provider path. This reduces error-rate in canary to ~1.8% (down from 12%) but adds ~150ms p99 latency for canary requests.
3) Cached recent DNS answers at our edge for the brightline domain to avoid repeated resolution delays for short TTLs.

Next: need Brightline ops to confirm if they changed recursive resolvers or applied any firewall/proxy updates this morning. Also request CloudPeers to provide BGP/peering snapshots for the window.

Attachments referenced: packet_capture_brightline_20260822.pcap | route_trace_brightline_20260822.txt

—Sean Gallagher
Network Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morales <alex.morales@brightlineretail.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Nitin Rao <nitin@cloudpeers.io>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 16:28:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Production errors and timeouts across checkout region (Brightline)

Alex — quick update for your ops and exec teams: we have identified a likely cross-provider peering degradation impacting DNS resolution and TCP path stability. Our engineers have deployed a temporary route bypass to a secondary model pool which has reduced errors for the canary set.

Immediate ask from Brightline: please confirm whether you applied any DNS or firewall changes between 13:30–15:00 UTC. If you can share (a) the IP range of your recursive resolvers and (b) any recent ACL changes, we can coordinate with CloudPeers to validate BGP and peering adjacencies.

We will continue monitoring and will avoid a global failover unless you authorize it — the bypass reduces errors but increases p99 latency, so we want to align on tradeoffs.

If you'd like, our CRO/ops can set up a short bridge in the next 20 minutes.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Leadership Team <leadership@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Executive summary — Brightline outage window & remediation actions (for exec visibility)

Leadership — brief summary for your visibility.

Timeline:
- 2026-08-22 14:02 UTC: Brightline reports checkout 5xx spike and latency.
- 14:00–15:30 UTC: DNS lookup times spike; traceroute indicates asymmetric path with a mid-hop in the CloudPeers backbone adding significant RTT and packet loss.
- 14:45 UTC: Temporary route bypass to secondary model pool deployed for canary traffic — error rate dropped from ~12% to ~1.8% for canary.

Root cause (interim):
- Primary indicator is a cross-provider peering/backbone degradation affecting Brightline's recursive resolvers and the mid-transit hop. No evidence of a Redwood origin bug.

Customer impact: checkout failures for ~12% of sessions at peak; revenue minutes affected for ~90 minutes. Brightline requested immediate mitigations and wants a hold on SLA credits until a post-mortem is complete.

Actions completed:
- Network performed route bypass and edge DNS caching.
- Opened CloudPeers ticket (JIRA-INC-7821) and requested BGP snapshots and peering logs for the window.
- Requested Brightline confirm their resolver IPs and firewall changes.

Next steps:
1) CloudPeers to provide BGP/peering evidence and confirm mitigation plan.
2) Joint RCA call with Brightline & CloudPeers scheduled if CloudPeers confirms a peering incident.
3) Prepare customer-facing RCA and internal post-mortem. Legal & Finance to standby for SLA/credit conversations.

Attachments: packet_capture_brightline_20260822.pcap | route_trace_brightline_20260822.txt

If leadership wants, I can prep a one-page memo for the board and the customer execs.

— Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
